policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Ketiv ויושיביני and qere וַיּוֹשִׁיבַנִי carry the same lemma (3427) and the same morphology (HC/Vhw3ms/Sp1cs); the difference is orthographic. ASV "and set me on the throne of David my father" renders both identically and carries no mapped textual note here, so nothing in the target distinguishes the readings. Retain the qere base that MACULA projects.
